BiblicalUsage: A seret is an incision, a cutting in the flesh, and the law forbids it twice over: ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor print any marks upon you, for I am the LORD. And the priests shall not make baldness upon their head, nor shave the corner of their beard, nor make any cuttings in their flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: The body is not ours to mark for the dead: grief does not cut, and mourning does not print.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
